data.command: What security tools do you have deployed?

data.text:
We've got a few security tools running in the background to keep things secure. I've got Fail2Ban configured to watch for and block brute-force login attempts on SSH and other services. It's been a lifesaver, let me tell you. We also have a decent setup of Snort and Suricata running as IDS/IPS to catch any potential threats. We've also got some custom scripts in place to monitor system logs and detect any suspicious activity.

As for intrusion detection, we've got OSSEC installed to monitor system calls and detect potential security incidents. It's a great tool for real-time monitoring and alerting. We've also got a Nessus scanner running periodically to scan for vulnerabilities in our system and services.

Of course, we've also got all the standard Linux security features turned on, like SELinux in enforcing mode and AppArmor for process confinement. We've also got our system logs rotated and monitored with a combination of logrotate and ELK (Elasticsearch, Logstash, Kibana) setup.

We've also set up a robust firewall configuration using UFW (Uncomplicated Firewall) to block unnecessary traffic and control access to our services. All this, combined with some good old-fashioned system hardening, should keep our system pretty
